closest.title: Bounded Rationality for LLMs: Satisficing Alignment at Inference-Time
closest.how_close: The closest methodological match. SITAlign maximizes helpfulness subject to harmlessness thresholds using KL-regularized constrained decoding and Lagrangian duality. Its approximate optimal multipliers depend on the current prompt and generated prefix. However, its thresholds are predefined; it does not demonstrate complexity-dependent safety budgets or per-prompt LARA calibration on a small calibration set.

closest.title: Safety Game: Inference-Time Alignment of Black-Box LLMs via Constrained Optimization
closest.how_close: Optimizes helpfulness over finite response candidates under a per-prompt safety cap, using a bounded-multiplier/game formulation and inference-time optimization. This overlaps with constrained Best-of-N selection, but uses game-based candidate mixtures rather than LARA calibration and does not establish complexity-adaptive thresholds or token-level decoding.

closest.title: Controllable Safety Alignment: Inference-Time Adaptation to Diverse Safety Requirements
closest.how_close: Shares the goal of changing safety requirements at inference time while preserving helpfulness. It trains models to follow natural-language safety configurations supplied through system prompts, rather than recalibrating Lagrangian multipliers or applying augmented rewards during reranking and decoding.

closest.title: SafeInfer: Context Adaptive Decoding Time Safety Alignment for Large Language Models
closest.how_close: Provides context-adaptive safety intervention during decoding, combining demonstration-derived activation steering with safety-guided token distributions. The intervention mechanism differs substantially: it does not use constrained helpfulness optimization with calibrated dual variables.

rationale: Very close work exists outside the bibliography, particularly SITAlign: it already combines the same helpfulness–harmlessness target with constrained inference-time decoding and context-dependent Lagrange multipliers. Safety Game additionally overlaps with per-prompt constrained response selection. However, I found no paper demonstrating the candidate's complete combination of safety thresholds that change with prompt complexity, per-prompt dual recalibration using a small calibration set, and application to both Best-of-N and token-level decoding. Adaptive multipliers alone do not establish adaptive constraint thresholds. LARA and InferenceGuard were excluded because they are already in references.txt. The evidence therefore supports substantial overlap with a remaining methodological distinction, rather than an exact prior implementation.
